title: Macutteris
summary: Macutteris is a Flatlands placename identified from a May 13, 1664 deed for upland and marshes in what is now Brooklyn. It appears in the same deed context as Hoopaninak and Shanscomacocke.
address_label: General Flatlands / Jamaica Bay marsh area, Brooklyn, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general Flatlands and Jamaica Bay marsh point based on Tooker's 1664 Flatlands deed context; offset slightly from Hoopaninak and Equendito for map visibility, not an exact marsh boundary.
translation_content:
Macutteris is related to Narragansett moskituash, meaning a meadow. His interpretation connects the name with the deed's marshland context rather than with a later neighborhood name.

Why Place Names Matter

“Every place name is assigned for a specific reason and time thus, and each name bears a unique story.”

— Angeline Awuor Oluoch, A Morpho-semantic Study of Toponyms in Dholuo (2022), PDF page 1, introduction
land_loss_content: Macutteris preserves a marshland name within a Flatlands deed that also records other Indigenous placenames. Mapping it separately helps show that beaches, islands, marshes, and enclosed water edges were named parts of a connected Canarsie landscape.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general Flatlands and Jamaica Bay marsh-area point, offset slightly from nearby Hoopaninak and Equendito markers for visibility. It does not mark an exact seventeenth-century marsh boundary.
